changes.description: Updated HB 156 status — initial federal challenge (Equality State Policy Center v. Gray) dismissed without prejudice July 2025; law in effect. Added four more 2025 session laws listed by the Secretary of State - HEA 62 (voter list maintenance and SAVE verification), HEA 71 (ranked-choice voting ban), SEA 10 (unsolicited absentee request forms), and SEA 75 (email notice of registration cancellation)

recentLegislation.description: Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote, and establishes a new durational residency requirement: voters must have resided in Wyoming for at least 30 days before an election.
recentLegislation.status: Became law without governor's signature; effective July 2025; federal challenges (including Equality State Policy Center v. Gray) dismissed on standing grounds in July 2025; law remains in effect

idRequirements.toRegister: DC driver's license or DMV-issued ID number, or last 4 of SSN. If neither, leave blank; must show ID when first voting (government-issued photo ID, utility bill within 90 days, bank statement, paycheck, or government document with name and address). For same-day registration, proof of residency required (university housing statements and off-campus leases explicitly accepted).
idRequirements.toVote: ID not required for registered voters (first-time voters who registered by mail may need ID)

registrationDeadline: Same-day registration available through election day

earlyVoting.details: Early voting begins 8 days before election day at designated vote centers.

mailInVoting.details: All registered voters automatically receive a mail ballot. No excuse required.

felonyVotingRules: No disenfranchisement. Incarcerated individuals may vote (DC restored voting rights for all citizens regardless of conviction status in 2020).
documentationNeeded: DC DMV ID number or last 4 of SSN
Proof of residency for same-day registration
notes: DC allows incarcerated individuals to vote. As a federal district, DC residents have no voting representation in Congress.
